articles.title: Install
articles.sub: about fifteen minutes, once
articles.html:
$ brew install python ffmpeg uv git rubberband
$ git clone https://github.com/drtranceypants/hypnomix && cd hypnomix
$ uv venv && uv pip install -e . && source .venv/bin/activate
$ uv pip install -e ".[plugins]"     # optional: render through your own plug-ins (lesson 11)
$ hypnomix doctor                     # checks every part and says what is missing
  1. For the Live features, run hypnomix install once and restart Live, then pick AbletonOSC as a Control Surface in Live's settings (Link, Tempo & MIDI).
  2. For the Max for Live devices (Live Suite, or Live with the Max for Live add-on): hypnomix device and hypnomix probe device put them in your User Library. They appear in Live's browser under User Library → Presets → Audio Effects → Max Audio Effect → Hypnomix.
  3. Start the app with hypnomix app. It opens in your browser and runs only on your computer.

articles.title: Teach it your style
articles.sub: so it proposes what you would do · and tells you where you could do better
articles.html:
Before your first review, let hypnomix study the songs you've already finished. It reads every Live set on your computer (it skips backups, factory packs and older versions of the same song) and your exported bounces. Nothing is rendered and nothing leaves your Mac. A few hundred sets take well under a minute, and after that only the sets you've changed are read again.

What it learns: how loud you set each kind of track against the lead vocal, how wide you pan, how much reverb and delay each part gets, which devices and plug-ins you use on what, how you set your compressors, EQs and limiters, what you automate, and how loud and bright your released songs are. A setting you keep the same in every song becomes a standard that tools stick to. One that changes from song to song is a taste call, and you'll be asked about it.

$ hypnomix taste --library                   # every set on this computer
$ hypnomix taste --library "~/Music/Projects"  # or just one folder
→ LIBRARY.md
# Your style, learned from your library
Learned from 9 sets in 24 s; 341 .als files found, 332 skipped (backups, packs, older versions).
## YOUR STYLE
- harmony: -5.9 dB against the lead (songs from -8.5 to -2.3 dB) · taste call
- centred in every song: bass, drums, harmony, lead · standard
- lead: reverb send -14.2 dB; delay send -12 dB
- bass: Compressor, Utility, EQ Eight (3 songs)
## WHERE YOU COULD IMPROVE
1. Bounces peak above -1 dBTP: three releases at -0.07, -0.5 and -0.62 dBTP.
   Streaming encodes add 0.5-1 dB, so they may clip after upload: try a -1 dB ceiling.
2. Compressor release faster than two bass cycles: 30 ms on a bass whose lowest
   note needs 61 ms. Try a longer release so it doesn't distort the low end.
3. Loudness differs by 4 LU between your songs: choose one target for the album.

Not sure of a song's genre? It guesses and asks you to confirm: hypnomix taste --library --genre "Song=folk". Once genres are set, your style is also broken down by genre.

articles.title: The first pass
articles.sub: scan · hear · decide · apply · all in the app
articles.html:
1. Songs: choose a Live set, or a folder of recordings from any DAW. A bounce of the mix and the key are optional and add loudness and tuning checks. Press Start the first pass. It only reads.
  2. Activity: every check runs at once (names, timing, clips, vocals, effects, the mix), then the before/after clips are made. You can watch or walk away.
  3. Review: one card per finding, most important first. Each has the problem in plain words, the proposed fix, and A and B players at matched loudness. Choose Approve, Skip or Change (with a note).
  4. Apply: writes only what you approved into one new set next to your original, then measures again to show what changed and what is still there.

articles.title: Decide faster, stay in charge
articles.sub: fewer clicks for the small things · every big thing still asked
articles.html:
• Amount. Approve a fix at 60% instead of all or nothing. It works for tuning, fades, clip gain, level and volume moves, device settings and timing nudges. Fixes that can't be scaled say so.
  • Apply to the ones like this. Decide one small click fix and apply the same decision to the 14 like it, after seeing the list. Anything you decided one by one stays as you decided it.
  • Why. With teaching on (the default), each finding explains the technique in two or three sentences: why a fade stops a click, why a slower release keeps the bass round.
  • A question budget. Tell it how many questions you want per song. The rest go into a "low priority" batch with a suggested decision for each group.
$ hypnomix fix "hypnomix-out/scan/Song" --decide tune-Lead=approve@60
$ hypnomix fix "hypnomix-out/scan/Song" --decide-like smooth-3=approve --dry-run   # see what it matches first
$ hypnomix prefs set review.max_questions=12 review.teach=on

articles.title: Review with someone
articles.sub: a co-producer, a bandmate, a client
articles.html:
Every decision records who made it and when. A reviewer can leave a note at a bar or a time on any finding. Send them the review file, and when it comes back, merge it: where you both decided the same finding differently, it's shown to you to settle. Your own decision is never overwritten without you seeing it.

$ hypnomix review "hypnomix-out/scan/Song" --export "Song review.json"     # send this
$ hypnomix review "hypnomix-out/scan/Song" --as Sam --serve              # they review as "Sam"
$ hypnomix review "hypnomix-out/scan/Song" --merge "Song review (Sam).json"
$ hypnomix review "hypnomix-out/scan/Song" --settle smooth-4=mine      # settle a conflict

articles.title: History and undo
articles.sub: every applied version is kept · undo writes a new set, it never deletes

$ hypnomix history "Song" --diff 2 3            # what changed between two versions
$ hypnomix history "Song" --undo-item tune-Lead  # the latest version without one fix
$ hypnomix history "Song" --undo 2               # go back to version 2 (as a new set)

articles.title: Tell it in Live
articles.sub: what each track is, and what the song is · no more guessing
articles.html:
1. Drag HypnomixProbe onto the last slot of one track and HypnomixMain onto Main. Save the set.
  2. Run hypnomix probe insert "Song.als". It writes a new set with a probe on every track, return and group (each starting at "auto").
  3. Set the menus where you know better than a guess. They're Live parameters, so they're saved in your set, and the next scan reads them. Leave "auto" anywhere you're happy for hypnomix to work it out by sound.
Modes such as Dorian or Mixolydian are tuned with the notes of their parent major key, so A Dorian is tuned to the notes of G major. Chords you type are kept by the app, matched to the song by its track names.

articles.title: Measure while you play
articles.sub: every track at once, after all of its plug-ins · no renders, no exports
articles.html:
The probe measures each track ten times a second, after every device and plug-in on it, which is what you actually hear. A full scan used to render each track without its effects. Now one play of the song measures them all, third-party plug-ins included. Press Record in the Live tab, play the song (or just the part you're working on), press Stop, and you get a normal review:

  • frequency fights between tracks while they play together, with the band and who should give way (your priority settings decide)
  • the lead vocal's level against the band, section by section
  • a low end that isn't mono, a mix that's too wide or narrow
  • Main's loudness and peak against your song card
  • tracks running hot into the next plug-in
$ hypnomix probe status                         # who's sending, loudness right now
$ hypnomix probe listen --bars 49-64 --play     # Live plays the chorus; a review comes back

articles.title: A/B inside Live
articles.sub: every fix as a switch · instant, with all your plug-ins, level-matched
articles.html:
1. In the review, press Build A/B set for Live (or run hypnomix abset). It writes one new set where every proposed fix sits next to what you have, switched off: a copy of the changed device named "B · …", or a muted copy of the track with the clip fixes.
  2. Close your set, open the A/B set, and put the hypnomix device on any track. It follows the review in the app, and Live jumps to each finding.
  3. Press A · now and B · fix while it loops. With the probe on Main and Match on, B is turned up or down to A's loudness, so you're judging the change and not just the level.
  4. Not sure? Press Blind: X and Y are A and B in a random order. Choose the one you like, and only then does it tell you which was which. The review shows how often you chose the fix.
The A/B set is for listening only. Approving still happens in the review, and Apply still writes the real new set from your original.

articles.title: Review before export
articles.sub: one button on Main
articles.html:
Press Record and review before export on HypnomixMain. Live plays, and the device records Main exactly as you hear it (a real-time bounce) while every probe listens. When Live stops, the app reviews it: loudness and true peak against your song card, the live findings, release checks, how it translates to phones, earbuds, cars and streaming codecs, and the mastering moves it would make, as proposals. Fix what you agree with, then export from Live as usual.

The device can't press Export for you, because Live doesn't let any device start an export. The recording it makes is the same audio a real-time export gives, and you can use it as the bounce for every other tool.

articles.title: Your real plug-ins, offline
articles.sub: render a track through the chain you built, faster than real time
articles.html:
With the optional plugins extra, hypnomix loads your VST3 and AU plug-ins outside Live and restores each one to the settings saved in your set. That way it can render a track through its actual chain, and the before/after clips for device changes include your plug-ins too. Each plug-in is tried in a separate process first, so one that crashes is reported and skipped and the render carries on.

$ hypnomix plugrender "Song.als" --list             # each chain, and what can be rendered
$ hypnomix plugrender "Song.als" --check            # load and restore every plug-in, no audio
$ hypnomix plugrender "Song.als" --tracks "Lead Vox" "Bass"
$ hypnomix ab "hypnomix-out/scan/Song" --plugins    # before/after for device fixes, through the chain
Live's own Utility, Compressor, Glue Compressor and Limiter are modelled. Other Live devices, racks and Max for Live devices are skipped and named in the report. Some Audio Units refuse to load outside a DAW; when a plug-in also comes as a VST3, that version is used instead.

articles.title: Mastering
articles.sub: options and fine controls · every move logged with why
articles.html:
optionwhat it does
tonal build · tonal checka target tone range from your releases or songs you choose; where your mix sits outside it
--amount 0-100scales every mastering move: 100 is the full proposal, 50 is half of each
--stabilize TARGETslow dynamic EQ that moves a band back toward the target only when it drifts out
--dyneqyour own dynamic EQ bands: frequency, threshold, ratio, width
--width-bands · --mono-belowstereo width per frequency range; a mono low end
--limiter-mode clean|punch|loudthe limiter's character; every run reports loudness gained against punch lost
--harsh · harshfinds and gently tames build-ups in the 2–6 kHz range only where they happen
--ditherproper dither on 16- and 24-bit files
rebalanceturn the vocal, bass or drums up or down inside a finished stereo mix
translate --previewhear it as MP3 and AAC, and as a streaming service plays it
$ hypnomix tonal build "Release 1.wav" "Release 2.wav" "Release 3.wav" --name mine
$ hypnomix tonal check "Song mix.wav" --target mine
$ hypnomix master "Song mix.wav" --target -11 --limiter-mode punch --stabilize mine --amount 80 --plan
$ hypnomix rebalance "Song master.wav" --vocals +1.5
$ hypnomix translate "Song master.wav" --preview

articles.title: Vocals
articles.sub: doubles and harmonies that sit together · your feel kept
articles.html:
vocalign lines doubles and harmonies up with the lead in time. If you ask, it also matches pitch and formant, checking each note against the chord under it. Presets cover the usual jobs, and you can protect any bars you want left exactly as sung. Inside Live, alignset writes the timing as warp markers on your own clips in a new set, and the Hypnomix Align device does it from inside Live.

$ hypnomix vocalign --list-presets
$ hypnomix vocalign "Lead.wav" "Double.wav" "Harmony hi.wav" --preset natural-double --protect 33-36
$ hypnomix vocalign "Lead.wav" "Harmony hi.wav" --pitch --chords "Song instrumental.wav"
$ hypnomix alignset "Song.als" --guide "Lead Vox" --parts "Double" "Harmony Hi" --apply   # warp markers on your own clips, in a new set
$ hypnomix aligndevice                  # the Align device for Live

articles.title: Faster every time
articles.sub: only what changed is looked at again
articles.html:
$ hypnomix scan "Song.als" --quick                 # structure, edges, levels: seconds, no rendering
$ hypnomix scan "Song.als" --since "hypnomix-out/scan/Song"   # only the tracks you changed
$ hypnomix watch "Song.als"                        # every time you save in Live, a quick check of what changed

Rendered clips are cached by their source file and settings, so a second scan of the same song re-renders nothing it has already rendered. The library scan, the names and the pitch analysis are cached the same way.

articles.title: What it is
articles.sub: an engineer, an assistant and a pair of hands on your Live set
articles.html:
hypnomix is a free, open-source mixing and mastering engineer that lives on your Mac and works with Ableton Live. It was built by Dr. Trance, who writes, plays, records, mixes and masters every part of his own music, for people who record real instruments and vocals, not just MIDI.

You can use it three ways. First pass: point it at a Live set, or a folder of recordings from any DAW. It runs every check at once, changes nothing, and writes one review list with before-and-after clips. You approve, skip or change each item, and only the approved fixes go into a new set next to your original. Engineer mode: give it a folder of stems and it cleans them up, balances them, compresses, EQs, pans, adds reverb and masters the result, then writes MIX NOTES.md explaining every decision. Hands-on mode: keep your own session and let hypnomix set exact fader levels and plug-in parameters in the open Live set, record A/B loops, and measure what each change did.

How it decides. Everything is measurement plus the rules an engineer would use. There are no black-box models in the mixing chain, so every decision can be written down and argued with. It measures; it doesn't listen. Treat its work as a strong first pass by an assistant, then make the taste calls yourself.

It learns how you work. It asks your preferences once (loudness target, tracks never to touch, what is deliberate), reads your own finished songs to learn your habits (how far your harmonies sit under the lead, how you pan, which effect moves you draw), and remembers what you approve and skip. Proposals then start from your standards, not from someone else's numbers.

It keeps the performance human. Timing fixes move only the hits that are clearly out, and only part of the way. Tuning moves the centre of a note and keeps the vibrato and slides. A full snap to the grid is refused.

It never needs a paid plug-in. Its own processing is built in, and anything it does offline it can also build inside Live from the stock devices every Live Standard or Suite owner already has.

articles.title: The app and the Live device
articles.sub: no terminal, no AI, no API key · the whole first pass by clicking
articles.html:
The web app. One command opens it in your browser; it runs on your computer only. Choose a Live set, or a folder of recordings from any DAW, and press one button: it runs every check and builds the before-and-after clips. The review shows each finding with play buttons for A and B and three choices: Approve, Skip, Change. Apply writes only what you approved into a new set next to your original, then shows exactly what changed. Your preferences and every other hypnomix tool are a click away, each with a form.

The Live device. A Max for Live device you drop on any track; audio passes through it untouched. It shows the finding you are on and steps through them, and Live jumps to each one: the track is selected, the playhead moves to the spot, the loop brace goes around it and the clip opens. Approve or skip right there. "Show in Live" buttons in the app do the same jump. The device never edits the set it sits in: applying still happens in the app, into a new set.

Both run on your computer only. Nothing is sent anywhere, and the app refuses requests from other sites. The device is new and needs Max for Live (Live Suite, or the add-on).

New: measure every track while Live plays, tell hypnomix what each track is and what the song is, A/B every fix inside Live with a blind test, and record a review before export. See the Training page for step-by-step lessons with pictures and videos.

$ hypnomix app          # opens http://127.0.0.1:8791 in your browser
$ hypnomix device       # optional: puts the Max for Live device in your Live User Library

Optional: make it a Mac app

Prefer an icon in your Dock to a browser tab? You can build your own Hypnomix.app: a small window around the same web app, which starts and stops it for you. It takes about a minute, and you build it yourself so it is made for (and trusted by) your own Mac.

1. Install Apple's command line tools once, if you haven't: xcode-select --install.
2. In the hypnomix folder, run macapp/build.sh.
3. Open macapp/dist/Hypnomix.app, or drag it into Applications.

If you move or reinstall the hypnomix folder, run the build again. The web app and the Mac app are the same thing inside; use whichever you like.

$ xcode-select --install     # once
$ cd hypnomix && macapp/build.sh
$ open macapp/dist/Hypnomix.app

articles.title: Install
articles.sub: about fifteen minutes, most of it downloads
articles.html:
1. Install Homebrew (skip if you have it)

    Homebrew installs the free tools hypnomix needs. Open Terminal (Applications → Utilities) and paste the line from brew.sh, then follow its prompts.

  2. Install the tools

    $ brew install python ffmpeg uv git
$ brew install blackhole-2ch rubberband   # recommended: recording from Live, best vocal re-timing

  3. Download and install hypnomix

    $ git clone https://github.com/drtranceypants/hypnomix && cd hypnomix
$ uv venv && uv pip install -e .
$ source .venv/bin/activate          # do this in each new Terminal window
$ hypnomix                            # prints the command list

    No uv? python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -e . does the same.

  4. Connect it to Ableton Live

    $ hypnomix install

    This copies the bundled AbletonOSC remote script into Live's User Library and walks you through the rest, including the two-minute BlackHole setup. Then restart Live and choose Settings → Link, Tempo & MIDI → Control Surface: AbletonOSC.

    To reach more of your plug-ins' parameters: hypnomix install --plugin-params (adds one line to Live's Options.txt; restart Live).

  5. Check everything

    $ hypnomix doctor

    It checks Live, AbletonOSC, BlackHole, ffmpeg and plug-in parameter access, and tells you what to fix.

  6. Optional extras

    extraaddsinstall
    referencehypnomix reference (Matchering; GPL-3.0, kept separate so hypnomix stays MIT)uv pip install -e ".[reference]"
    mlseparate (split a song into stems) and midi (audio → MIDI)uv pip install -e ".[ml]"
    critiquea written second opinion from Gemini (needs GEMINI_API_KEY)uv pip install -e ".[critique]"

  7. Updating later

    $ cd hypnomix && git pull && uv pip install -e .

articles.title: How to use it
articles.sub: ten recipes that cover most sessions · everything lands in hypnomix-out/ with a Markdown report next to the audio
articles.html:
1 · Mix a folder of stems, start to finish

$ hypnomix automix "Night Drive stems/" --name "Night Drive" --reference "reference.wav"
$ hypnomix translate "hypnomix-out/automix/Night Drive/Night Drive (master).wav" --render
$ hypnomix qc "hypnomix-out/automix/Night Drive/Night Drive (master).wav"

Read MIX NOTES.md, listen on headphones and a phone, and change what your ears disagree with: usually vocal level and reverb amount.

2 · Master a finished mix

$ hypnomix master "Song mix.wav" --target -14
$ hypnomix master "Song mix.wav" --target -14 --reference "reference.wav" --match 0.6
$ hypnomix chain master "Song bounce.wav" --target -14 --verify --existing bypass   # same, built in Live

3 · Clean up raw recordings

$ hypnomix prep "raw stems/"
$ hypnomix dehiss "Lead Vox.wav" --reduce 12 --gate 18 --report
$ hypnomix vocalign "Lead.wav" "Double.wav" "Harmony hi.wav" --trim-tails --level -6

4 · First pass on a Live set: scan → hear → review → fix

$ hypnomix prefs                                                    # once: targets, protected tracks
$ hypnomix scan "Song.als" --mix "Song mix.wav" --key "F# major"   # read-only → REVIEW.md
$ hypnomix scan "Song.rpp"                                          # or a REAPER project
$ hypnomix scan "Song/"                                             # or an Ardour session folder
$ hypnomix scan "raw takes/"                                        # or a folder from any DAW
$ hypnomix ab "hypnomix-out/scan/Song"                              # before/after clips, level-matched
$ hypnomix review "hypnomix-out/scan/Song" --serve                  # a page: play A, play B, click
$ hypnomix fix "hypnomix-out/scan/Song" --approved --out "Song (fixed).als"

Every check runs at once, nothing changes until you approve it, and approved changes land in one new set next to the original, which fix then checks and measures again to confirm each problem is gone. Close the set in Live before fix.

5 · Hands on your open set

$ hypnomix live snapshot                                   # always first
$ hypnomix live db "Lead Vox" -3.5
$ hypnomix live paramd "Lead Vox" "EQ Eight" "1 Frequency A" 2500
$ hypnomix loop --bar 49 --bars 8 --ab "db Bass -1.5" --revert   # the A/B habit

6 · Recording a part

$ hypnomix soundcheck --watch --device "USB Audio"     # set the preamp: peaks -12 to -6 dBFS
$ hypnomix live input "Gtr" "Ext. In" "2" && hypnomix live arm "Gtr" 1
$ hypnomix live record 17 8 3                          # bars 17–24, three takes
$ hypnomix takes "Gtr take 1.wav" "Gtr take 2.wav" "Gtr take 3.wav" --bpm 92

7 · A harmony stack that sits right

$ hypnomix voices --learn "Finished song 1.als" "Finished song 2.als"   # your own spacing, once
$ hypnomix voices "Lead.wav" "Harmony lo.wav" "Harmony hi.wav"           # lists the parts and asks
$ hypnomix voices "Lead.wav" "Harmony lo.wav" "Harmony hi.wav" --anchor lead --tame
$ hypnomix tune "Lead.wav" --ref "Song mix.wav" --key "F# major" --report-only

8 · A drum take played without a click

$ hypnomix tempomap "Drum take.wav" --click "check.wav"       # listen: is the click on the beat?
$ hypnomix tempomap "Jam.als" --track "Drums" --conform --preview "conformed.wav" --apply "Jam (conformed).als"
$ hypnomix tempomap "Jam.als" --track "Drums" --follow --apply "Jam (tempo map).als"   # or: the grid follows the drummer
$ hypnomix loops "Jam.als" --track "Drums" --apply "Jam (loops).als"                  # best loops into Session slots

9 · Tighter, but still played by a person

$ hypnomix timing "Song.als" --track Drums --track Bass --track Guitar    # only the hits out of time with the band
$ hypnomix tighten "Song.als" --track "Drums" --strength 0.5 --preview "tighten preview/"
$ hypnomix breathe "Song.als" --mix "Song mix.wav" --preview "Song (breathing).wav"    # choruses push, verses relax

10 · A song that loops too much

$ hypnomix variations "Song.als"                              # unused takes that fit; A/B files to audition
$ hypnomix variations "Song.als" --apply "Song (variations).als"   # new tracks, switched off
$ hypnomix borrow "Song.als" --mix "Song mix.wav" --plan    # loops the original project had
$ hypnomix motion --learn "Finished song.als"                # your own effect moves, once
$ hypnomix motion "Song.als" --mix "Song mix.wav" --plan    # risers, dips, throws: options to approve

Everything in recipes 8 to 10 arrives as an option: a preview file, a switched-off track, or an item in the review. Turn it on, listen in the mix, keep or delete.

Numbers cheat sheet

whattargetwhy
Recording peaks (24-bit)-12 … -6 dBFSheadroom for the loud take; noise is irrelevant at 24-bit
Noise between notesbelow -60 dBFSabove -50 is audible once compressed
Stems into a mix~-20 LUFS playing, peaks ≤ -3 dBFSplug-ins behave; faders near 0
Pre-master mix~-18 LUFS, peaks ≤ -3 dBFSroom for the master chain
Master for streaming-14 LUFS, ≤ -1 dBTPmatches platform playback, codec-safe
Limiter reductionunder ~2 dB transparentmore means fix the mix
Vocal stack timingunder 10 ms tight, 20–40 ms naturalabove that, flams
Low end below 120 HzL/R correlation > 0.9mono-, club- and vinyl-safe

articles.title: With an AI agent
articles.sub: optional · ask for the mix in plain English, from the cloud or fully offline on your Mac
articles.html:
hypnomix is a set of terminal commands that write plain-text reports, so any AI coding agent that can run commands in a folder can drive it. Open the hypnomix folder in your agent and ask for what you want:

"Mix the stems in ~/Music/Bounces/Night Drive. Make it sound like this reference."
"I'm about to record acoustic guitar on input 2. Set up a track and check my levels."
"Do a first pass on ~/Music/Song Project/Song.als. The mix is Song.wav."
"Master this for Spotify and check it'll survive on a phone."

Rather not use a cloud AI at all? You don't have to. See Run your own AI, free and offline below.

What the agent gets. AGENTS.md in the repo is written for any agent: setup, the loop every job follows, the safety rules (ask your preferences first, scan before changing anything, one item at a time with you, new files only, measure again afterwards), the command map and how to extend the code. The skills/ folder holds six ready-made workflows (first-pass, harmony-balance, mix-engineer, mastering-engineer, tracking-session, live-mixing), and docs/LESSONS.md lists the real mistakes the rules come from, so your agent doesn't repeat them. Agents with skill support load them directly; any other agent can read them as plain instructions.

Building inside Live. The included MCP config connects the open-source Ableton MCP (telemetry off), so agents that speak MCP can create tracks and load devices, and rebuild an automix inside your set from recipe.json.

Set up a track and check my levels." "Do a first pass on ~/Music/Song Project/Song.als. The mix is Song.wav." "Master this for Spotify and check it'll survive on a phone." Rather not use a cloud AI at all? You don't have to. See Run your own AI, free and offline below. What the agent gets. AGENTS.md in the repo is written for any agent: setup, the loop every job follows, the safety rules (ask your preferences first, scan before changing anything, one item at a time with you, new files only, measure again afterwards), the command map and how to extend the code. The skills/ folder holds six ready-made workflows ( first-pass , harmony-balance , mix-engineer , mastering-engineer , tracking-session , live-mixing ), and docs/LESSONS.md lists the real mistakes the rules come from, so your agent doesn't repeat them. Agents with skill support load them directly; any other agent can read them as plain instructions. Building inside Live. The included MCP config connects the open-source Ableton MCP (telemetry off), so agents that speak MCP can create tracks and load devices, and rebuild an automix inside your set from recipe.json .

articles.title: Run your own AI, free and offline
articles.sub: no data center, no subscription, no closed model: an open-weight model on your own computer
articles.html:
Maybe you'd rather not feed the data-center boom. Maybe you want your music and your tools to stay open source, end to end. Maybe a monthly AI subscription just isn't in the budget. All good: hypnomix doesn't need any of it. You can run an open-weight model on your own machine, driven by an open-source agent, and nothing ever leaves your computer.

Our recommendation: gpt-oss:20b, an open-weight model under the Apache 2.0 licence that's built for tool use (running commands, reading reports, trying again), served by Ollama (free) and driven by OpenCode (free, open source). It runs on a computer with 16 GB of memory or more, which covers most recent Macs with Apple silicon and many PCs. The download is about 14 GB.

Only 8 GB? Use a smaller model such as qwen3:8b in the same steps. It's lighter but less reliable on long jobs, so give it one command at a time.

  1. Install Ollama

    Ollama downloads and runs open models on your computer. Get the Mac app from ollama.com/download (or Ollama.dmg directly), drag it to Applications and open it. Or, in Terminal:

    $ curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh

  2. Download the model

    $ ollama pull gpt-oss:20b          # about 14 GB, one time

  3. Give it room to think

    Agents need a long memory (the "context length"). Ollama defaults to a short one on most computers, and agents need at least 64,000. In the Ollama app, open Settings and drag the context-length slider to 64k. Or start Ollama from Terminal with it set:

    $ OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=64000 ollama serve   # quit the Ollama app first if it's open

    A longer context uses more memory. If things crawl, check ollama ps: the PROCESSOR column should say 100% GPU.

  4. Install OpenCode, the agent

    OpenCode is a free, open-source agent that runs in Terminal. Install it with the one-line command on opencode.ai/docs.

  5. Start it on hypnomix

    $ cd hypnomix
$ source .venv/bin/activate
$ ollama launch opencode --model gpt-oss:20b

    Then just ask: "Run hypnomix doctor and tell me what's missing," or "Master Song mix.wav to -14 LUFS and check it on a phone." The agent reads AGENTS.md, runs the commands and reads the reports. (Already running OpenCode? Type /models and pick gpt-oss:20b; it finds Ollama by itself.)

Honest expectations. A local model is slower than a cloud one and makes more mistakes on long, multi-step jobs. hypnomix is built for that: every command writes a report, scan changes nothing, and fix only applies what you approve. A small model can take it one step at a time while REVIEW.md does the remembering. And you can always skip the AI and type the commands yourself; every one is on this page.

articles.sub: the slow, technical jobs · found for you, explained in plain words, fixed only with your yes
articles.html:
the chorewhat hypnomix doescommands
Hunting clicks, pops and level jumpsFinds clicks at clip edges and loop seams, jumps where one comped clip cuts to the next, plosives and spikes, and eases each with a short fade or dip. It also catches the opposite mistake: a fade or comp edit that cuts into a word.smooth edges clicks
Finding the hit that's lateDetects the song's own grid (straight, triplets or a mix), locks the low end first (bass to the drums), compares every hit with the rest of the band, and nudges only the clear outliers part of the way. Drums go first, then the bass toward the corrected drums, then everything else. Audio gets warp markers you can still drag; MIDI drums and bass are checked too.timing tighten unroll
Tuning a vocal note by noteMeasures the song's real tuning and key (section by section), then moves only each note's centre. Vibrato, scoops and slides stay as sung. Where the key is unsure it asks, and leaves those notes alone until you answer.tune key
Lining up doubles and harmoniesWorks word by word: only the words clearly out of time with the other parts are moved, the rest stay bit-exact.vocalign
Balancing a harmony stackLists each part with its note and level, asks which one leads, and turns down only the parts that overshadow it, by the amount you pick or the spacing you use in your own finished songs. It is judged as heard, after each track's effects, and written as volume automation.voices cliplevel
Chasing hiss, hum, breaths and "s" soundsSpectral de-hiss, hum and rumble removal, breaths turned down (not off), a split-band de-esser that lists every "s" it touched, clipped peaks rebuilt.prep dehiss deess breaths
Finding what's distortingClipped takes, drive set too hot, limiters working too hard, compressors releasing faster than a bass note: each named with its track, bar and a setting to try.distortion
Setting up sidechains and duckingMeasures how deep each sidechain ducks and whether it recovers in time, proposes settings for the style you want, and can make the vocal reverb and delay step back while the singer sings.sidechain duck
Naming, ordering and tidying 40 tracksNames every track by how it sounds, puts them in working order (drums, bass, keys and guitars, vocals) and puts each harmony on the track for its pitch, so one fader is one voice. Switched-off old takes are retired after a full archive copy of the set is saved.name order tidy
Checking every compressor and gatePlays each track through its own chain and judges every stock device on the signal it really gets: a compressor that barely works, squashes, or lets go too fast for a bass note; a gate that chops words. It suggests threshold, attack and release for that part and tempo.devices
Mapping a take played without a clickFollows the beat through the take, writes a click check for your ears, then either warps the take onto the grid or makes Live's tempo follow the player. It also picks the best loops and lines them up to try.tempomap loops
Making a looped song feel aliveSmall tempo pushes into choruses, filter sweeps and delay throws in the style of your own automation, and unused takes or loops from the original project offered on new, switched-off tracks.breathe motion variations borrow
Working out which parts clashWhich two parts fight over which frequencies, how often, and the exact cut that fixes it. Mic pairs checked for phase and polarity.masking align stems
Getting loud without wrecking itA mastering chain set by measurement, test-encoded to AAC and MP3 so it won't clip after upload, built offline or inside Live from stock devices.master chain
The pre-release checklistPhone, earbuds, car and mono checks; how much each streaming service will turn it down; silence, true peak, phase and format. Section by section: "the second chorus is 2 LU quieter than the first".translate qc sections match

What stays yours: the playing, the sounds, the effects, the arrangement and every taste call. hypnomix asks before anything that changes how the song feels, shows what is deliberate (your automation, your long reverb tail) on every review so nobody "fixes" it, and never overwrites a file.

articles.title: What it can do
articles.sub: all 83 commands, grouped the way you'll use them · run hypnomix <command> -h for full options · new = passes its tests and the structure check, still young: keep your original and listen
articles.html:
First pass

scan a song, hear each fix, approve, apply

appnew
The whole first pass in a window: choose a song, hear each fix, approve, apply. No terminal and no AI needed.
devicenew
A Max for Live device: step through the findings inside Live, and Live jumps to each one.
prefs
Asked once: your loudness targets, tracks to protect, what is deliberate, and how you like to review. It remembers what you usually approve and skip.
scan
Runs every check on a Live set, a REAPER project, an Ardour session, or a folder of recordings or stems from any DAW. Changes nothing. Writes REVIEW.md, most severe first, and lists any check that could not run.
projectnew
Looks inside a REAPER project or an Ardour session without opening the DAW: tracks, buses, items or regions, takes, plug-ins and automation. --render renders each track to a full-length file.
reapernew
Talks to the REAPER that is open: starts the bridge, lists tracks, installed plug-ins and their parameters.
ab
Before-and-after clips for each proposed fix, at matched loudness, so you hear it before you approve it.
review
The whole review as one page: play A, play B, click approve, skip or change. Approve part of a move with an amount, decide the ones like this together, read why each technique works, leave notes, and merge a collaborator's review.
fix
Applies only what you approved into one new set, then measures it again to show which problems are gone. Refuses a set that changed since the scan, never overwrites a file, asks again before a protected track.
check · diff
Every set hypnomix writes gets a structure check before you open it, and a plain list of what changed. Tracks are matched by id, so a new order or new names show as expected changes, not errors.
taste
Reads your own finished songs: fader levels against the lead, panning, reverb and delay amounts, device chains, what you automate. What you always do becomes a standard; what varies becomes a question. --library studies every set on your computer at once (in seconds after the first run) and adds where you could improve, with the evidence.
profile
Your sound as measured ranges, from songs you love.
historynew
Every version fix wrote for a song: list them, see what changed between two, undo to any version or rebuild without one fix. Undo always writes a new set.
watchnew
Keeps an eye on a set while you work: every time you save, a quick check of only what changed. Read-only.

Clean-up in the set

the first tidy of a session, without opening Live

name
Names every track and group by how it sounds: drums, bass, guitar, strings, lead vocal, harmonies, keys, pads.
ordernew
Tracks in working order, and each part of a vocal stack on the track for its pitch. Never changes the sound.
tidynew
Retires switched-off tracks (after an archive copy with every take) and puts one instrument's clips on one track. Clips may overlap only where the overlap is silence, which is cut away: no sound is ever overwritten.
devicesnew
Checks every stock compressor, gate, limiter and EQ low cut by what it does to its track, and suggests settings.
smooth
Clicks at clip edges and loop seams, level jumps at cuts, and real pops: eased with short fades and dips. A consonant that opens a sung phrase is left alone; plosives get at most 3 dB.
timing
Detects the song's grid (straight, triplets or mixed), finds hits out of time with the band and nudges only those, part of the way. In passes: drums, then bass toward the drums, then the rest. Audio and MIDI.
distortion
Audible distortion in takes and device chains (clipped takes, hot drive, fast bass compression), with a fix for each.
sidechain
Measures every sidechain's ducking (depth, recovery, timing) and suggests settings for clarity, pump or vocal ducking.
ducknew
Vocal reverb and delay that step back while the singer sings and bloom in the gaps: tunes what you have, or adds it.
cliplevelnew
Finds single harmony clips sitting far under the rest of their track and offers a clip-gain raise.
unrollnew
A looped clip becomes one copy per pass, so a single pass can be nudged or changed on its own.
automation
List, show, offset or dip automation envelopes.
mine · audit · refs
Tempo, key, plug-in chains and routing; stacked limiters and bypassed devices; missing audio files.

Vocals & recordings

real instruments, real voices

prep
Raw takes → mix-ready stems: clicks, clipping, plosives, breaths, hum, hiss, silence, fades, gain staging. --plan turns every repair into an item you approve.
tune
Extremely gentle pitch correction to the song's own tuning: a 35% nudge, only notes over 20 cents off, never more than 25 cents, and only the moved notes are replaced. From a Live set it tunes the takes under your comp clips, so the comp stays yours.
key
The song's key with a confidence, mapped section by section; names the one disputed note when it is unsure.
edgesnew
Finds the start of a word your comp loses: an “s” or “t” the take sings but a fade or a comp edit turns down, only where the word goes on right after. Fixes are clip edits on your own comp (a shorter fade, an earlier start, a later comp switch), re-checked until clean.
vocalign
Doubles and harmonies in time with each other, word by word, with presets, protected areas and sync points; optional pitch matching (chord-checked) and formant.
alignset · aligndevicenew
Aligns the vocal parts inside a Live set as warp markers on your own clips, in a new set; or from the Hypnomix Align device in Live.
voices
Balances harmonies around the part you choose, or splits them into one track per voice. --learn reads the spacing you use in your own songs; in a set it is judged as heard and written as volume automation.
dehiss · deess · breaths
Spectral de-hiss with a smart gate; a split-band de-esser; breaths turned down, not off. Each reports before it writes.
clipmatch
Evens out clips recorded at different gain or mic positions.
takes
Ranks takes by clipping, noise, pitch and timing; writes a comp list per section.
soundcheck
Listens to your input and tells you how to set the preamp. --watch is a live meter.
cleanup
Demo rescue: hum, noise, rumble, DC, silence.

Tempo, feel & variety

keep it human, keep it moving

tempomapnew
Follows the beat of a take played without a click. Then warps the take to the grid, or makes the grid follow the take. A click check comes first.
loopsnew
The best 1, 2, 4 and 8 bar loops in a free-played take, grouped by groove, lined up in Session slots to try.
tightennew
A gentle quantise: hits move part of the way to the click, close ones stay put, a full snap is refused.
breathenew
Small tempo changes by section for a song recorded to a rigid click, with a preview of your mix bent along the new tempo.
motionnew
Risers, filter dips, reverb swells, delay throws, stutters and drop-outs for repetitive sections, in the lengths and depths of your own automation. Options only.
variationsnew
Unused takes of a part that fit the loop it keeps repeating, on a new switched-off track next to it.
borrownew
Loops the song's original project had and the new version dropped, offered as switched-off layers that fit the key and groove.

Engineer

stems in, song out

automix
Stems folder → balanced mix + master, with notes on every move. --plan lists each EQ, compressor, level and pan move for approval first.
master
Stereo mix → release master at a loudness target, or matched to a reference. Codec-safe. Options: a tonal stabilizer toward your own target, dynamic EQ, width by band, limiter character (clean, punch, loud), harshness taming, dither, and an amount for everything. --plan stage by stage.
rebalancenew
Turns the vocal, drums or bass up or down inside a finished stereo mix, true-peak safe.
chain
Builds the mastering chain (or per-track channel strips) inside Live from stock devices and dials in every value. --reaper builds it in REAPER from its stock plug-ins.
masking
Which stems fight over which frequencies, and the exact cut that fixes it.
align
Phase, polarity and time offset between mics on one source (kick in/out, DI + amp).
translate
Mono, phone, earbuds and car checks; streaming loudness; clipping after MP3/AAC encoding. --preview to hear it as MP3, AAC, and at the level a streaming service plays it.
qc
Release checklist: format, silence, true peak, loudness, phase. Exits 1 on failure.

Ears

measure and compare

measure
Loudness, true peak, bands, stereo, tempo and key → JSON.
sections
Finds the song's sections; loudness and vocal balance in each.
match
Your mix against a song you love, as proposals: tone by band, dynamics, width, loudness.
tonalnew
A target tone range built from your own released songs (or ones you choose), and where a mix sits outside it, with the EQ move and a plot.
harshnew
Lists the moments with a harsh 2–6 kHz build-up, with timestamps; master --harsh tames only those.
spectrogram
Spectrogram, loudness curve and average spectrum as a PNG.
pitchcheck · clicks
Pitch and loudness difference between two captures; clicks and crackle in renders.
punch
Transient punch, pumping and harmonics A/B at matched loudness.
stems
Who owns which band (and any resonance) in a folder of stems.
referenceextra
What it would take to sound like a reference (Matchering).
separate · midiextra
Split a finished song into stems; audio → MIDI, and into a Live clip.
critiqueextra
A written second opinion on a mix from a cloud AI model (Gemini; needs your own API key).

Inside Live

Max for Live devices · no renders, no exports

probenew
HypnomixProbe on every track measures it after all its plug-ins while Live plays: one play of the song is a deep scan. Tell it what each track is, its priority and whether it's protected. HypnomixMain on Main holds the song card (genre, key, scale, chords, loudness target, ceiling, limiter character) and records Main for a review before export.
absetnew
Every proposed fix as a switched-off B next to what you have, in one new set: the hypnomix device switches A, B and a blind test instantly, with all your plug-ins and matched loudness.
plugrenderextra
Renders tracks offline through your real VST3 and AU plug-ins, restored from the settings saved in your set, so before/after clips include your chain.

Live

hands on the open set, through AbletonOSC

live
Faders in exact dB, sends, pans, mute and solo; any device or VST/AU parameter in real units; transport; snapshots; input routing, arming and punch recording with take lanes.
loop
Plays bars, records them, measures them and compares. --ab "db Lead -2" --revert for one-change A/Bs.
diagnose
Solos every group in the loudest section: who owns the sub, the bass and the vocal band.
render
Not Live at all: renders a set's tracks to stems with Live closed, following every warp marker, pitch preserved.
install · doctor
Installs the Live remote script; checks Live, AbletonOSC, BlackHole, ffmpeg and plug-in parameter access.

How automix decides, move by move

movethe rule behind it
RolesReads each stem's name first (kick, snr, bass, gtr, keys, vox, bv, pad…), then the sound. Name your stems: it's the single best thing you can do for the result.
Clean-up EQHigh-passes parts with nothing useful down low (vocals and guitars ~90 Hz, hats ~300 Hz); cuts resonances only when present in most of the song; wide cuts for mud (200–500 Hz) and harshness (2.5–5 kHz).
Tone EQOnly where needed: kick weight at 60 Hz and click at 4 kHz, bass harmonics around 800 Hz for small speakers, vocal presence at 3 kHz and air at 10 kHz.
CompressionSet by result, not threshold: vocal ~5 dB at 3:1, bass ~5 dB at 4:1, drum bus ~2 dB at 2:1. The vocal gets a split-band de-esser after it.
BalanceFrom each part's loudness while it is sounding: lead vocal on top, kick ~3 dB under, bass and snare ~4, guitars and keys ~7, pads ~12.
PanningKick, snare, bass and lead centred; doubles, backing vocals and keys spread in pairs; low end kept mono.
MaskingTwo parts fighting in the same band at the same time: the less important one gives way with a 2–3 dB cut. The lead vocal is never the one cut.
Space & glueOne shared plate (1.8 s, 25 ms pre-delay) puts everything in one room; kick and bass stay dry. Drums glued at 2:1, 30 ms attack, ~2 dB.

The mastering chain

stepwhat and whyin Live (stock)
1 · SubsonicHigh-pass at 22 Hz: energy no speaker plays still eats limiter headroom.EQ Eight
2 · Tone matchOptional: moves your tonal balance part of the way (default 60%, capped ±3 dB) toward a reference.EQ Eight
3 · Glue1.5:1, slow attack, ~1.5 dB. More than ~2 dB becomes an effect.Glue Compressor
4 · Mono lowsBelow 120 Hz, only if the low end is wide.Utility
5 · WarmthOptional saturation so bass is heard on small speakers.Saturator
6 · LimiterTrue-peak limiting to the loudness target, 4× oversampled.Limiter
7 · Codec-safeTest-encodes AAC 256 and MP3 320; lowers the ceiling if they'd clip.Limiter ceiling
8 · Top & tailHead silence trimmed to 50 ms, a 3 ms fade-in, a fade-out if the song ends abruptly.

Approve part of a move with an amount, decide the ones like this together, read why each technique works, leave notes, and merge a collaborator's review. fix Applies only what you approved into one new set, then measures it again to show which problems are gone. Refuses a set that changed since the scan, never overwrites a file, asks again before a protected track. check · diff Every set hypnomix writes gets a structure check before you open it, and a plain list of what changed. Tracks are matched by id, so a new order or new names show as expected changes, not errors. taste Reads your own finished songs: fader levels against the lead, panning, reverb and delay amounts, device chains, what you automate. What you always do becomes a standard; what varies becomes a question. --library studies every set on your computer at once (in seconds after the first run) and adds where you could improve, with the evidence. profile Your sound as measured ranges, from songs you love. history new Every version fix wrote for a song: list them, see what changed between two, undo to any version or rebuild without one fix. Undo always writes a new set. watch new Keeps an eye on a set while you work: every time you save, a quick check of only what changed. Read-only. Clean-up in the set the first tidy of a session, without opening Live name Names every track and group by how it sounds: drums, bass, guitar, strings, lead vocal, harmonies, keys, pads. order new Tracks in working order, and each part of a vocal stack on the track for its pitch. Never changes the sound. tidy new Retires switched-off tracks (after an archive copy with every take) and puts one instrument's clips on one track. Clips may overlap only where the overlap is silence, which is cut away: no sound is ever overwritten. devices new Checks every stock compressor, gate, limiter and EQ low cut by what it does to its track, and suggests settings. smooth Clicks at clip edges and loop seams, level jumps at cuts, and real pops: eased with short fades and dips. A consonant that opens a sung phrase is left alone; plosives get at most 3 dB. timing Detects the song's grid (straight, triplets or mixed), finds hits out of time with the band and nudges only those, part of the way. In passes: drums, then bass toward the drums, then the rest. Audio and MIDI. distortion Audible distortion in takes and device chains (clipped takes, hot drive, fast bass compression), with a fix for each. sidechain Measures every sidechain's ducking (depth, recovery, timing) and suggests settings for clarity, pump or vocal ducking. duck new Vocal reverb and delay that step back while the singer sings and bloom in the gaps: tunes what you have, or adds it. cliplevel new Finds single harmony clips sitting far under the rest of their track and offers a clip-gain raise. unroll new A looped clip becomes one copy per pass, so a single pass can be nudged or changed on its own. automation List, show, offset or dip automation envelopes. mine · audit · refs Tempo, key, plug-in chains and routing; stacked limiters and bypassed devices; missing audio files. Vocals & recordings real instruments, real voices prep Raw takes → mix-ready stems: clicks, clipping, plosives, breaths, hum, hiss, silence, fades, gain staging. --plan turns every repair into an item you approve. tune Extremely gentle pitch correction to the song's own tuning: a 35% nudge, only notes over 20 cents off, never more than 25 cents, and only the moved notes are replaced. From a Live set it tunes the takes under your comp clips, so the comp stays yours. key The song's key with a confidence, mapped section by section; names the one disputed note when it is unsure. edges new Finds the start of a word your comp loses: an “s” or “t” the take sings but a fade or a comp edit turns down, only where the word goes on right after. Fixes are clip edits on your own comp (a shorter fade, an earlier start, a later comp switch), re-checked until clean. vocalign Doubles and harmonies in time with each other, word by word, with presets, protected areas and sync points; optional pitch matching (chord-checked) and formant. alignset · aligndevice new Aligns the vocal parts inside a Live set as warp markers on your own clips, in a new set; or from the Hypnomix Align device in Live. voices Balances harmonies around the part you choose, or splits them into one track per voice. --learn reads the spacing you use in your own songs; in a set it is judged as heard and written as volume automation. dehiss · deess · breaths Spectral de-hiss with a smart gate; a split-band de-esser; breaths turned down, not off. Each reports before it writes. clipmatch Evens out clips recorded at different gain or mic positions. takes Ranks takes by clipping, noise, pitch and timing; writes a comp list per section. soundcheck Listens to your input and tells you how to set the preamp. --watch is a live meter. cleanup Demo rescue: hum, noise, rumble, DC, silence. Tempo, feel & variety keep it human, keep it moving tempomap new Follows the beat of a take played without a click. Then warps the take to the grid, or makes the grid follow the take. A click check comes first. loops new The best 1, 2, 4 and 8 bar loops in a free-played take, grouped by groove, lined up in Session slots to try. tighten new A gentle quantise: hits move part of the way to the click, close ones stay put, a full snap is refused. breathe new Small tempo changes by section for a song recorded to a rigid click, with a preview of your mix bent along the new tempo. motion new Risers, filter dips, reverb swells, delay throws, stutters and drop-outs for repetitive sections, in the lengths and depths of your own automation. Options only. variations new Unused takes of a part that fit the loop it keeps repeating, on a new switched-off track next to it. borrow new Loops the song's original project had and the new version dropped, offered as switched-off layers that fit the key and groove. Engineer stems in, song out automix Stems folder → balanced mix + master, with notes on every move. --plan lists each EQ, compressor, level and pan move for approval first. master Stereo mix → release master at a loudness target, or matched to a reference. Codec-safe. Options: a tonal stabilizer toward your own target, dynamic EQ, width by band, limiter character (clean, punch, loud), harshness taming, dither, and an amount for everything. --plan stage by stage. rebalance new Turns the vocal, drums or bass up or down inside a finished stereo mix, true-peak safe. chain Builds the mastering chain (or per-track channel strips) inside Live from stock devices and dials in every value. --reaper builds it in REAPER from its stock plug-ins. masking Which stems fight over which frequencies, and the exact cut that fixes it. align Phase, polarity and time offset between mics on one source (kick in/out, DI + amp). translate Mono, phone, earbuds and car checks; streaming loudness; clipping after MP3/AAC encoding. --preview to hear it as MP3, AAC, and at the level a streaming service plays it. qc Release checklist: format, silence, true peak, loudness, phase. Exits 1 on failure. Ears measure and compare measure Loudness, true peak, bands, stereo, tempo and key → JSON. sections Finds the song's sections; loudness and vocal balance in each. match Your mix against a song you love, as proposals: tone by band, dynamics, width, loudness. tonal new A target tone range built from your own released songs (or ones you choose), and where a mix sits outside it, with the EQ move and a plot. harsh new Lists the moments with a harsh 2–6 kHz build-up, with timestamps; master --harsh tames only those. spectrogram Spectrogram, loudness curve and average spectrum as a PNG. pitchcheck · clicks Pitch and loudness difference between two captures; clicks and crackle in renders. punch Transient punch, pumping and harmonics A/B at matched loudness. stems Who owns which band (and any resonance) in a folder of stems. reference extra What it would take to sound like a reference (Matchering). separate · midi extra Split a finished song into stems; audio → MIDI, and into a Live clip. critique extra A written second opinion on a mix from a cloud AI model (Gemini; needs your own API key). Inside Live Max for Live devices · no renders, no exports probe new HypnomixProbe on every track measures it after all its plug-ins while Live plays: one play of the song is a deep scan. Tell it what each track is, its priority and whether it's protected. HypnomixMain on Main holds the song card (genre, key, scale, chords, loudness target, ceiling, limiter character) and records Main for a review before export. abset new Every proposed fix as a switched-off B next to what you have, in one new set: the hypnomix device switches A, B and a blind test instantly, with all your plug-ins and matched loudness. plugrender extra Renders tracks offline through your real VST3 and AU plug-ins, restored from the settings saved in your set, so before/after clips include your chain. Live hands on the open set, through AbletonOSC live Faders in exact dB, sends, pans, mute and solo; any device or VST/AU parameter in real units; transport; snapshots; input routing, arming and punch recording with take lanes. loop Plays bars, records them, measures them and compares. --ab "db Lead -2" --revert for one-change A/Bs. diagnose Solos every group in the loudest section: who owns the sub, the bass and the vocal band. render Not Live at all: renders a set's tracks to stems with Live closed, following every warp marker, pitch preserved. install · doctor Installs the Live remote script; checks Live, AbletonOSC, BlackHole, ffmpeg and plug-in parameter access. How automix decides, move by move move the rule behind it Roles Reads each stem's name first (kick, snr, bass, gtr, keys, vox, bv, pad…), then the sound. Name your stems: it's the single best thing you can do for the result. Clean-up EQ High-passes parts with nothing useful down low (vocals and guitars ~90 Hz, hats ~300 Hz); cuts resonances only when present in most of the song; wide cuts for mud (200–500 Hz) and harshness (2.5–5 kHz). Tone EQ Only where needed: kick weight at 60 Hz and click at 4 kHz, bass harmonics around 800 Hz for small speakers, vocal presence at 3 kHz and air at 10 kHz. Compression Set by result, not threshold: vocal ~5 dB at 3:1, bass ~5 dB at 4:1, drum bus ~2 dB at 2:1. The vocal gets a split-band de-esser after it. Balance From each part's loudness while it is sounding : lead vocal on top, kick ~3 dB under, bass and snare ~4, guitars and keys ~7, pads ~12. Panning Kick, snare, bass and lead centred; doubles, backing vocals and keys spread in pairs; low end kept mono. Masking Two parts fighting in the same band at the same time: the less important one gives way with a 2–3 dB cut. The lead vocal is never the one cut. Space & glue One shared plate (1.8 s, 25 ms pre-delay) puts everything in one room; kick and bass stay dry. Drums glued at 2:1, 30 ms attack, ~2 dB. The mastering chain step what and why in Live (stock) 1 · Subsonic High-pass at 22 Hz: energy no speaker plays still eats limiter headroom. EQ Eight 2 · Tone match Optional: moves your tonal balance part of the way (default 60%, capped ±3 dB) toward a reference. EQ Eight 3 · Glue 1.5:1, slow attack, ~1.5 dB. More than ~2 dB becomes an effect. Glue Compressor 4 · Mono lows Below 120 Hz, only if the low end is wide. Utility 5 · Warmth Optional saturation so bass is heard on small speakers. Saturator 6 · Limiter True-peak limiting to the loudness target, 4× oversampled. Limiter 7 · Codec-safe Test-encodes AAC 256 and MP3 320; lowers the ceiling if they'd clip. Limiter ceiling 8 · Top & tail Head silence trimmed to 50 ms, a 3 ms fade-in, a fade-out if the song ends abruptly.

articles.sub: questions people ask
articles.html:
Is hypnomix free?

Yes, free and open source under the MIT licence. It never needs a paid plug-in. The tip jar is optional.

Do I have to use a terminal or an AI?

No. hypnomix app opens a web app on your own computer that does the whole first pass by clicking (you can also build it into your own Mac app): choose a song, listen to each proposed fix, approve, apply. The Max for Live device lets you step through the findings inside Live. Installing hypnomix itself still takes a few terminal lines, once. More about the app.

Do I need Ableton Live?

Only for the Live features: controlling the open set, recording, and building device chains. The file tools (prep, automix, master, vocalign, tune, dehiss, translate, qc and more) work on audio files without Live.

Does it work on Windows?

It's built and tested on macOS. The file tools and Live control should work on Windows, but that's untested.

Will it mess up my Live set?

It saves a mixer snapshot before changing anything (hypnomix live restore undoes it), never deletes your plug-ins, and the scan → fix workflow writes approved changes into one new set while your original stays untouched. Every set it writes is checked for structural problems before you open it; one that fails is renamed so it can't be opened by accident. fix refuses to run if the set changed since the scan, never overwrites a file, and asks again before touching a track you marked as protected.

Will it quantise my playing or auto-tune my voice?

No. Timing tools move only the hits that are clearly out of time, and only part of the way; a full snap to the grid is refused. Tuning moves each note's centre toward the song's own tuning and keeps vibrato, scoops and slides. Every one of those changes is an item you approve, with a before-and-after clip.

How does it know what I like?

It asks once (hypnomix prefs), learns from your own finished songs (taste, voices --learn, motion --learn, profile) and remembers what you approve and skip in each review. All of it stays in a folder on your computer.

I use REAPER or Ardour

Point scan straight at the project: hypnomix scan "Song.rpp", or an Ardour session folder (Ardour 3 to 9). It reads the tracks, buses, takes or regions (as Ardour layers them), fades, plug-ins and automation, and runs the same checks as on a Live set. The DAW can stay open; nothing is written next to your project. For now, changes that belong in the project are listed for you to make there; repaired audio comes back as new files.

I use Logic, Pro Tools or something else

Export each track as a full-length file from the same start point and run hypnomix scan "that folder/". The review works the same way; repaired audio comes back as new files, and anything that has to happen in your DAW is listed as a to-do. Reading and writing other DAWs' projects is on the roadmap.

Is it AI?

The mixing and mastering decisions are measurement plus the rules an engineer would use; there are no black-box models in the mixing chain, so every move is written down with its reason. You can drive it with any AI agent if you like, including one running entirely on your Mac, and the optional critique command can ask a cloud model for a second opinion.

Can I use it with AI but without paying for AI, or without a data center?

Yes. Run an open-weight model on your own computer with Ollama and drive it with the open-source OpenCode agent: free, offline, and nothing leaves your machine. We recommend gpt-oss:20b on computers with 16 GB of memory or more. Step-by-step setup here.

Will it replace a mixing engineer?

Treat it as a very fast assistant's first pass. It measures; it doesn't listen. The taste calls are yours, or hire a human, or learn the craft in one-on-one lessons.

Where do the files go?

Into hypnomix-out/ in the folder you run it from (set HYPNOMIX_OUT to change it). Every tool writes a Markdown report next to its audio.

Something isn't working

Run hypnomix doctor first; it names what's missing. Then open an issue on GitHub.
